title: Register changes that correct the E02A claim, V2-S7-004-PR1
description: What V2-S7-004-PR1 changed in the register after an independent adjudication ruled that no source that predates the first fault of V2-E02A settles the meaning of E02A-AC2, and after the repository owner chose the verdict not-decided on 2026-11-02: every register change with its value before and after, the finding each answers, and the review artifacts the changes rest on. It is the eighth ledger written after v1.0.0 was released, and like the seven before it, it is not part of the pack that release was cut over: the evidence index undoes it, with the other post-release ledgers, to recompute that pack. It narrows the statement of one claim, appends a dated correction to its limitation, adds to what the claim does not establish, sets the outcome of E02A-AC2 to not-evaluated in each of the three records, corrects each summary and two limitations of each record, adds six cited files to each record, and replaces one surface reason. It adds no claim and no record, moves no status and no evidence level, raises and closes no blocker, declares no freeze, states no release, and edits no dated record and no earlier ledger. The earlier wording stays in the ledger that added the claim, and here as the value before the change. The list of ledgers is in tools/evidence_index, a pinned input of the latest freeze records, so this ledger moves those pins, and no revision classifies them yet.

registerChanges.before: In three runs on 2026-10-31, on the docker-desktop provider, on one cluster with one node, at the commit ff45093b2a9bf2cdbcde5fee453fbc6b64f2e53b, under revision 4 of the V2-E02A freeze record, a release with two API replicas and one runtime replica served the real model while the RP-1 caller sent requests through the API Service, and the control deleted the one runtime pod once in each run. In each run two requests failed, in one failure episode of 3,682 ms to 4,276 ms that the analysis starts about 30 s after the fault, and the largest time between two successes is 29,893 ms to 30,427 ms. The seven validity criteria of the record hold in each run, on the reading of E02A-AC2 that the repository owner approved after the evidence was read, so each is PASSED, which states that the run is valid and not that the service stayed available. The set meets the comparison eligibility rule of the record on its failure episodes.
registerChanges.after: In three runs on 2026-10-31, on the docker-desktop provider, on one cluster with one node, at the commit ff45093b2a9bf2cdbcde5fee453fbc6b64f2e53b, under revision 4 of the V2-E02A freeze record, a release with two API replicas and one runtime replica served the real model while the RP-1 caller sent requests through the API Service, and the control deleted the one runtime pod once in each run. In each run two requests failed, in one failure episode of 3,682 ms to 4,276 ms that the analysis starts about 30 s after the fault, and the largest time between two successes is 29,893 ms to 30,427 ms. Each manifest states PASSED, which is not a statement that the service stayed available. The validity of the three runs is not established, because no source that predates the first fault settles the meaning of E02A-AC2, and the current comparison eligibility verdict is not-decided.
registerChanges.reason: The statement said that the seven validity criteria hold and that the set meets the eligibility rule. An independent adjudication ruled that no source that predates the first fault settles the meaning of E02A-AC2, and the repository owner chose the verdict not-decided on 2026-11-02. Both sentences are withdrawn. What executed and each measured figure stay word for word.

registerChanges.before: Runtime, C2, about three runs, e02a-1, e02a-2, and e02a-3, at one commit, on one provider, docker-desktop, on one cluster with one node on Kubernetes v1.36.1, with one release, one model, and one caller workload. The state of each run rests on a reading of E02A-AC2 that the repository owner approved on 2026-10-31, after the evidence was read: the freeze record does not state that reading, no tool reads the approval, and on the readings of the runtime readyReplicas count no run would be counted and this claim would not stand. The eligibility rests on the failure episodes alone. The zero-Ready condition holds on the first reading that gave zero and not on the outer start, and the record does not state which applies. The start of a failure episode is the completion of its first failed request: the failed requests were in flight for most of the time with no completion, and the caller failure episode does not hold that time. The failure count is 2 in each run, and the caller profile has 2 workers. The model file of each replacement pod was not compared directly. The host paged, and no record establishes whether that changed a figure. The review of the result is a record of a separate session of the same assistant, and no person and no outside party reviewed the result. It read no register statement about these runs, it ran no tool of this repository, and it does not establish that this claim is correct. Registration, 2026-11-01: V2-S7-001-PR2 ran the three runs and registered no claim. V2-S7-002-PR1 classified them and added this claim. No run executed in that change, and no file of a run changed.

The failure count is 2 in each run, and the caller profile has 2 workers. The model file of each replacement pod was not compared directly. The host paged, and no record establishes whether that changed a figure. Registration, 2026-11-01: V2-S7-001-PR2 ran the three runs and registered no claim. V2-S7-002-PR1 classified them and added this claim. No run executed in that change, and no file of a run changed. Correction, 2026-11-02: until V2-S7-004-PR1 the statement of this claim gave each validity criterion as held and gave the verdict of the classification record as the current verdict. An independent adjudication ruled that no source that predates the first fault settles the meaning of E02A-AC2, and the repository owner accepted that ruling and chose the verdict not-decided on 2026-11-02. docs/proof/experiments/v2-e02a/eligibility-adjudicated.v1alpha1.json states that verdict and what each reading gives on the raw streams: the reading scope holds in 3 of 3 runs, and the two runtime counts that the review chose after the evidence was read hold in 0 of 3, and no source selects them. The statement now states what executed and the measured figures, and those do not rest on either reading, so the claim status stays certified. Each manifest keeps PASSED and each attempt keeps counted: true, and neither establishes validity. A later approval does not make a post-result choice preregistered, and no criterion is rewritten. The adjudicator is an automated session and not a person, and its limits are in docs/proof/experiments/v2-e02a/eligibility-adjudication.v1alpha1.json.
registerChanges.reason: The limitation travels with the claim wherever it is shown. Two clauses that gave the old verdict are replaced, and the dated correction states what the earlier wording said, why it stopped being stated, and what stayed.

before.statement: The control deleted exactly the pod that the rule of fault.target selected (the first Ready runtime pod by name), once, by name: commands.txt holds one delete command, the fault-injection-started event names that pod, and a pods reading after the event shows that UID with a deletion timestamp or absent. No other pod of the release has a deletion timestamp before the end of the observation, except a pod that the Deployment controller removes.

The endpoints, pods, deployments, and argo streams are each accepted by their reader, each states a value in its first and its last reading inside the window, and each has at most 10 s between two consecutive readings with a value inside the window.

The caller record is accepted by its reader with the plan, in the mode in-cluster, with the API Service as its target and the end state duration. It covers the window, its last completion before the window succeeded, so the window does not start inside a failure episode, and at least one request completes inside the window after the fault-injection-finished event.

Either a pod of the tier of the fault with a UID that no pod had before the fault is Ready in a pods reading and the analysis states a stabilized recovery inside the observation limit, or the observation limit is reached. The result page states which.

When the analysis states a stabilized recovery inside the observation limit, at least 10 successful requests complete after the stabilizedAt instant inside the window, and the last of them completes at least 60 s after it.
No unrelated failure occurs inside the window: no container of a pod that the fault did not target restarts, no pod that the fault did not target is replaced, and the node stays Ready.

Every file that evidencePaths lists is present and named by the manifest, the operator event log is closed, python -m tools.experiment_evidence check accepts the run directory, and python -m tools.analysis_replay verify reproduces its run analysis.
